AuditConfig.description: Where the audit journal is written and the key its hashes are made with.

destination.description: Where audit entries go: a rotated `file` (the default) or `stdout`.

hashKeyRef.description: Secret reference to the audit hash key.

path.description: The absolute path of the active audit file, for `destination: file`.

retentionDays.description: How many days a sealed audit file is kept.

rotateBytes.description: The size at which the active file is sealed and a new one begun.

AuditDestinationKind.description: The configured audit destination kind, as written in product configuration.

oneOf.description: Durable, rotated JSON Lines file.
One JSON line per entry on standard output, flushed per entry.

CallbackBodyEncoding.description: How an `hmac-sha256-body` tag is encoded in its header.

CallbackVerifierConfig.description:
How the runtime authenticates one provider's inbound delivery callbacks,
closed and tagged by `type` in kebab-case.

oneOf.description:
HMAC-SHA1 over the full external callback URL with the request's form
parameters sorted by key and appended as `key` then `value` with no
delimiter, base64 in `header`. The `form-sms-gateway` example provider
package documents the provider scheme this matches.

url.description:
The external callback URL the provider was given and signs, as it
was given: scheme, host, any port, and path, without a query or
fragment. The route appends the request's own query string. A
proxy may rewrite what the runtime receives, so the runtime never
reconstructs this URL from the request.

oneOf.description:
HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body, encoded in `header` as
`encoding`.

A secret random token carried in the callback path, for gateways that
can only be given a URL.

CredentialPlacement.description: Where an OAuth client secret travels in the token request.

DatabaseConfig.description:
The PostgreSQL connection a stateful runtime uses. Both URLs are secret
references and may name the same secret.

migrationUrlRef.description: Secret reference to the migration connection URL.

runtimeUrlRef.description: Secret reference to the least-privileged runtime connection URL.

testOnlyPlaintext.description: Allow a plaintext connection. Refused outside test builds.

trustedRootCertificateRef.description:
Secret reference to a PEM root certificate the connection trusts.
Absent, the connection trusts the platform's root certificates.

Digest.description: A SHA-256 digest: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits.

EnvironmentSecretProviderConfig.description: The environment secret provider. It takes no settings.

root.description:
Absolute directory holding one file per secret. Each file must be a
regular file owned by the runtime user, mode 0400 or 0600, with exactly
one hard link.

HttpProviderAuthentication.description:
How a send authenticates to the provider, chosen by `type`. The
credential is added by Rust after the prepare script returns; no script
ever sees it.

oneOf.description: No credential. Only for a loopback development provider.
`Authorization: Basic` over the two resolved values.

`Authorization: <scheme> <token>`. Absent, the scheme is `Bearer`,
the only one the destination substrate presents today.
The resolved value in the named request header.

The resolved value in the named query parameter, appended after the
script's own target.

AWS Signature Version 4 for a JSON API. Rust signs the final request;
credentials are never exposed to provider scripts.

sessionTokenRef.description:
The session token for temporary credentials. Omitted, the request
is signed without one.

oneOf.description:
An OAuth 2.0 client-credentials bearer token, fetched from
`tokenEndpoint` and cached.

assumedLifetimeSeconds.description:
The lifetime assumed, in seconds, when the token response carries
no `expires_in`. Omitted, `expires_in` is required.

credentialPlacement.description:
Where the client secret travels. The token request carries it in
the form body; `basic-header` is refused until the substrate can
place it there.

maximumCacheSeconds.description: The longest a fetched token is reused, in seconds.

JwksSource.description: Where a runtime obtains the OIDC issuer's signing keys.

oneOf.description: Read `jwks_uri` from the issuer's OpenID Connect discovery document.
Fetch the key set from this absolute `https` URI, skipping discovery.

Read the key set from a secret, for deployments without network access
to the issuer.

ListenerBind.description: Socket address the runtime listens on, written host:port with an IP address host ([addr]:port for IPv6).

ListenerConfig.description: The listener of a runtime that declares no TLS or exposure settings.

ListenerNetworkExposure.description: The operator-declared private network placement of an HTTP listener.

LocalId.description: A local identifier: a lowercase letter, then up to 63 lowercase letters, digits, `_`, or `-`.

OidcConfig.description:
The OIDC issuer whose access tokens this runtime accepts, the clients it
admits, and the claim carrying their scopes.

allowedClients.description:
Client identifiers whose access tokens are admitted. A runtime decides
whether an empty list is acceptable in production.

assertionIssuers.description:
Assertion authorities each client may exchange a subject token from,
keyed by client identifier. An empty map applies no rule. Once a
client is listed, a token it exchanged is accepted only for one of
that client's declared authorities.

audience.description: The audience every accepted access token must carry in `aud`.

issuer.description:
Exact issuer accepted in access-token `iss` claims, an absolute
`https` URL.

jwksSource.description:
Where the issuer's signing keys come from. Absent reads the issuer's
OpenID Connect discovery document.

PackageConfig.description:
The package a runtime serves: `root` is the absolute package directory,
and `expectedDigest`, when set, pins the package digest the runtime must
find there. The package digest is the digest of the package's
`SHA256SUMS` file; see [`crate::package`].

expectedDigest.description:
`sha256:` label of the package digest, the digest of the package's
`SHA256SUMS` file. When set, the runtime refuses to start on any other
package.

root.description: Absolute path of the package directory.

PrivateListenerConfig.description:
The listener of a runtime that declares its TLS termination and network
exposure.

ProviderConnection.description:
One provider's runtime half. The package declares the provider's type,
and for an `http` provider its scripts; the two halves must name the same
type.

oneOf.description: One SMTP provider's runtime settings, as the operator writes them.

allowedPrivateCidrs.description:
Exact RFC 1918, CGNAT, or unique-local networks the relay may resolve
into. Every other non-public address is refused.

attemptTimeoutMilliseconds.description:
How long one attempt may take, from 1000 to 60000 milliseconds;
omitted, 30000.

host.description:
The relay's DNS name or IP literal. It is resolved once per attempt and
is the name TLS verifies the relay's certificate against.

port.description:
Defaults to 587 for `starttls` and 465 for `implicit`; required for
`development-loopback`.

trustedRootCertificateRef.description:
A PEM root certificate trusted in addition to the public web roots,
for a relay behind a private certificate authority.

oneOf.description: Runtime settings for one HTTP provider.

acknowledgeQueryStringContent.description:
Required, and only allowed, when the package sends with `get`: the
message content travels in the query string, where provider access
logs keep it.

allowedPrivateCidrs.description:
Exact RFC 1918, CGNAT, or unique-local networks an `https` provider may
resolve into, for an in-country gateway on a private network. Every
other non-public address is refused. Omitted, the provider may resolve
only to public addresses.

attemptTimeoutMilliseconds.description:
One send's whole budget in milliseconds: resolution, connection,
request, and response.

baseUrl.description:
The provider's origin and path prefix, ending in `/`. Every request
target a script returns is relative to it and stays under it.
`https` in production; `http` only to a loopback host.

callbackVerifier.description:
How the provider's delivery callbacks are authenticated. Required
exactly when the package declares `receipts: callback`.

maximumConcurrentRequests.description:
The most sends this deployment has in flight to the provider, at most
the package's declared `capabilities.maximumConcurrentRequests`.

maximumResponseBytes.description: The largest response body read, at most 1 MiB.

tlsTrustProfile.description:
The operator-declared trust bundle the provider's certificate may
chain to, by its name under `tlsTrustProfiles`. Its roots are trusted
in addition to the system roots, not instead of them. The runtime
resolves the name to PEM and passes it to
[`HttpProviderSettings::activate`].

RedirectPolicy.description: Redirect handling. A provider redirect is never followed.

RetentionConfig.description:
Retention periods the retention sweep enforces. Every value is deployment
configuration: a jurisdiction's retention schedule approves the deployed
numbers, and the audit journal records them at startup.

payloadRetentionDays.description:
How long a message's rendered payload and recipient contact are kept,
from 1 to 30 days.

recordRetentionDays.description:
How long the content-free message record is kept, at least as long as
the payload and at most ten years.

submissionReceiptRetentionDays.description:
How long a submission receipt stays replayable under its idempotency
key, from one day to the record period.

SecretProvidersConfig.description:
The secret providers a runtime enables. A reference is resolved only by a
provider declared here: `secret:file/name` under `file.root`, and
`secret:env/NAME` only when `environment: {}` is present.

environment.description:
Enables `secret:env/NAME` references, read from the process
environment. Declared as an empty mapping: `environment: {}`.

file.description: Enables `secret:file/name` references, read from files under `root`.

SecretReference.description: An exact secret reference: secret:file/name, resolved under secretProviders.file.root, or secret:env/NAME, resolved only when secretProviders.environment is declared.

SmtpAuthentication.description: The credential pair the relay authenticates, as `secret:` references.

SmtpTlsMode.description: How the connection to the relay is protected.

oneOf.description:
Connect in plaintext and upgrade with `STARTTLS` before anything else
is sent. The relay must offer it. Defaults to port 587.
TLS from the first byte. Defaults to port 465.

Plaintext to a loopback relay, for a local development server only.
The host must be a loopback literal or `localhost`, every resolved
address must be loopback, and the port must be explicit. Accepted
only by a test build or behind a `development-loopback` listener.

TlsTermination.description:
Declares the trusted transport boundary for a runtime's plaintext HTTP
listener. Production listeners require operator-controlled upstream TLS
termination; direct plaintext is limited to the explicit loopback-only
development mode.

TlsTrustProfileConfig.description:
A PEM bundle of one or more certificate authorities, held in the secret
provider so it is read under the same file checks as every credential.

Url.description: An absolute http or https URL with a host and no user information.

identity.description:
The logical database identity this deployment owns. It is independent of
the connection URL and PostgreSQL database name.

providers.description:
The runtime half of each package provider, by provider id: where the
provider is and how the runtime authenticates to it. A package
provider with no entry has no transport, and its messages fail with
`provider-unconfigured`.

tlsTrustProfiles.description:
Named PEM bundles an `http` provider's `tlsTrustProfile` trusts in
addition to the system roots, at most 64.
